channel.title: Eat Safe Japan — vegan
channel.description: Gluten-free, vegan, halal and allergy-friendly eating in Japan — explained by locals.

item.title: Shojin Ryori: Japan's Vegan Temple Cuisine Explained
item.description: Shojin ryori is Japan's centuries-old Buddhist temple cuisine, traditionally free of meat, fish and even onion and garlic. But modern versions vary. Here's how to tell the difference, where to find the real thing, and exactly what to ask before you eat — with the Japanese phrases to use at temple lodgings and restaurants.

item.title: The One Ingredient Vegetarians Miss in Japan
item.description: Dashi is the savoury stock behind miso soup, simmered vegetables, tamagoyaki and countless sauces in Japan — and it's usually made from fish. Learn what dashi is, why it's so hard to avoid, and how to ask for kombu or vegetable-based dashi instead. Includes exact Japanese phrases for restaurants.

item.title: Vegan Ramen in Japan: What to Know Before You Order
item.description: Ramen looks simple but the broth is almost always built on bonito or pork. Learn what makes ramen non-vegan, which styles are adaptable, and the exact Japanese phrases to ask staff about dashi and hidden animal ingredients.

item.title: Vegan in Japan: The Fish Stock Problem (and Fixes)
item.description: Travelling to Japan as a vegan? The biggest challenge isn't meat — it's dashi, the fish stock hidden in soups, sauces and even 'vegetable' dishes. Learn where it hides, which meals are easiest to adapt, how to read labels, and the Japanese phrases to ask staff.
